phase: Phase 3B.4: Authorization Runtime Verification & Phase 4 Gate

findings.title: Gate 0 Caller Role Confusion in SECURITY DEFINER Functions
findings.evidence: In PostgreSQL SECURITY DEFINER functions, CURRENT_USER evaluates to function owner ('postgres'), not the caller. Under initial implementation, unauthenticated callers entering with auth.uid() IS NULL triggered Guard 0.4.
findings.exploitability_impact: High. An authenticated student or unauthenticated caller executing via direct connection or PostgREST without auth.uid() could spoof p_admin_user_id.
findings.before_behavior: Evaluated CURRENT_USER IN ('postgres', 'service_role'), which always succeeded inside SECURITY DEFINER regardless of invocation context.
findings.after_behavior: Enforces SESSION_USER IN ('postgres', 'service_role') AND auth.role() IS NULL in Guard 0.4; explicitly rejects auth.role() = 'anon' in Guard 0.1; requires cryptographic auth.uid() in Guard 0.2.
findings.remediation: Updated migration.sql Gate 0 logic to check SESSION_USER and auth.role() nullity. Re-verified across all 18 database tests.
findings.residual_risk: None in database kernel. Re-verified in Phase 3B.4.

findings.title: Alternate Parent Write Path Integrity Bypass in Booklet & Option Mappings
findings.evidence: Updating parent occurrence_id on booklet_question_mappings or representation_id on question_options could orphan or cross-wire child options.
findings.exploitability_impact: High. Could corrupt answer key evaluation where options map to different questions than intended.
findings.before_behavior: Parent tables allowed occurrence_id and representation_id updates without verifying child option mapping presence.
findings.after_behavior: Triggers trg_booklet_qmap_occurrence_guard and trg_question_option_rep_guard block updates when child mappings exist, raising MCQJ-ERR-4008 and MCQJ-ERR-4009.
findings.remediation: Implemented parent mutation triggers in migration.sql and added NULL validation checks.
findings.residual_risk: None. Parent table updates are strictly constrained.

findings.title: Plaintext Test Database Credentials in Test Harness Output & Documentation
findings.evidence: Static test password was present in docker-compose.test.yml fallback and committed report tables.
findings.exploitability_impact: Medium. Credential hygiene risk and potential pattern reuse.
findings.before_behavior: docker-compose.test.yml defaulted to static fallback when TEST_DB_PASSWORD was unset.
findings.after_behavior: docker-compose.test.yml fails closed if TEST_DB_PASSWORD is missing (${TEST_DB_PASSWORD:?...}). Zero plaintext passwords across entire repository.
findings.remediation: Scrubbed all occurrences across 100% of repository files. Re-scanned and verified 0 occurrences.
test_references: Phase 3B.4 automated credential scanner: 0 matches found

findings.title: PostgREST Defense-in-Depth for Anonymous Role Privilege Bounds
findings.evidence: SQL REVOKE ALL FROM anon prevented PostgREST from exposing procedures to anonymous callers, but procedural bodies lacked internal defense-in-depth.
findings.exploitability_impact: Informational. Defense-in-depth against accidental future role grant mutations.
findings.before_behavior: Depended solely on SQL DDL GRANT/REVOKE statements.
findings.after_behavior: Added Guard 0.1 checking IF auth.role() = 'anon' THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'MCQJ-ERR-5015: Unauthorized: Anonymous callers cannot execute publication procedure'.
findings.remediation: Added Guard 0.1 to both administrative procedures.

findings.title: Formalization of Phase 4 Multi-Path Authorization Contracts
findings.evidence: Phase 4 implementation requires unambiguous contracts across Path A (PostgREST Client RPC with JWT), Path B (Next.js Server Action / Route Handler via Prisma direct connection), and Path C (Service Role / trusted background jobs).
findings.exploitability_impact: Informational. Prevents architectural mismatch and security regressions during Phase 4 UI and server action development.
findings.before_behavior: Integration tests only tested Path A (JWT claims) in DB-11.
findings.after_behavior: Added DB-18 verifying Path B direct execution, user role verification in users table, anti-spoofing guards, and Path C headless service-role fail-closed behavior.
findings.remediation: Formalized assertion contracts and implemented comprehensive DB-18 suite.

findings.title: Transaction Pooler Stale Context Isolation in Next.js Prisma Connections
findings.evidence: In production, Next.js connects via Prisma PgBouncer/Supavisor transaction pooler (port 6543). Session-level SET statements can leak across transactions on reused pooled connections.
findings.exploitability_impact: Low to Medium if session-level SET is used. Mitigated by direct parameter passing and database anti-spoofing guards.
findings.before_behavior: Guard 0.4 supported both current_setting('mcqj.caller_user_id') and p_admin_user_id.
findings.after_behavior: DB-18.11 verifies that if a pooled connection retains a stale session setting, passing a different admin UUID fails closed. Phase 4 contract mandates passing p_admin_user_id directly and forbidding session-level SET.
findings.remediation: Codified in Phase 4 implementation checklist and verified in DB-18.11.
findings.residual_risk: Low. Relies on adherence to Server Action parameter contract.

findings.title: Public Surface Exposure of Administrative Procedures via PostgREST
findings.evidence: migration.sql executes 'GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION ... TO authenticated', exposing publication and re-evaluation endpoints on the public PostgREST HTTP gateway (/rpc/fn_publish_exam_paper).
findings.exploitability_impact: Low. Guard 0.2 checks role = 'ADMIN' in users table and rejects students/contributors. However, public exposure creates unnecessary attack surface.
findings.before_behavior: Administrative procedures are visible on PostgREST schema.
findings.after_behavior: Administrative workflows in Phase 4 are executed strictly server-side via Next.js Server Actions connecting over Prisma (SESSION_USER = 'postgres'). Direct client RPC is not required.
findings.remediation: Recommend revoking EXECUTE from 'authenticated' in Phase 4 Module 1, reserving execute grants to 'service_role' and direct postgres.
findings.residual_risk: Low. Database role checks currently block non-admins.

findings.title: Account Suspension Boundary Between Supabase Auth and Database Role
findings.evidence: public.users schema does not contain an is_suspended column. Administrative revocation (role <> 'ADMIN') is enforced natively at the database level, while user suspension is enforced at the authentication layer via Supabase Auth banned_until.
findings.exploitability_impact: Low. Role demotions are immediately enforced by the database (DB-18.9). Account-level bans require session validation.
findings.before_behavior: Report examples referenced dbUser.isSuspended, which is not present in schema.prisma.
findings.after_behavior: Clarified that DB enforces role revocation natively, while account suspension must be verified via supabase.auth.getUser() and/or an added status column in Phase 4.
findings.remediation: Documented in Phase 4 Service Layer checklist and verified in DB-18.9.
findings.residual_risk: Low. Clarified contract prevents confusion during UI development.

documented_limitations: Tests executed against local disposable PostgreSQL 16 container with Supabase compatibility mocks (auth schema, JWT session variables). Remote Supabase PostgREST gateway, connection poolers, and live Supabase Auth tokens remain strictly un-mutated and will be verified during Phase 5 Production Readiness Gate.
The example assertAdminSession() and publishExamPaperAction() server functions do not yet exist in src/ and must be implemented as the first deliverable of Phase 4 Module 1.
